envelope_status: DESIGN_HYPOTHESIS_ONLY; literature context does not empirically bound these endpoints

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: seismic/deformation-zone extent, not a universal mechanical corridor width; not transferable as a measured ARCANA parameter
literature_evidence.reported_scale: up to several hundred kilometres wide
literature_evidence.source: Chen & Grimison (1989), Earthquakes associated with diffuse zones of deformation in the oceanic lithosphere: some examples

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: reported dimensions are not necessarily cross-boundary width; supports context dependence, not a numeric width bound
literature_evidence.reported_scale: some zones exceed 1000 km on a side
literature_evidence.setting: Global review, continental and oceanic diffuse boundaries
literature_evidence.source: Gordon (1998), The plate tectonic approximation: Plate nonrigidity, diffuse plate boundaries, and global plate reconstructions

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: supports finite-domain/strain representation; does not prescribe universal width, partition, or ARCANA constitutive law
literature_evidence.reported_scale: finite deforming network domains tessellated by triangular mesh
literature_evidence.source: Gurnis et al. (2018), Global tectonic reconstructions with continuously deforming and evolving rigid plates

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: technical capabilities only; no ARCANA physical or width authority
literature_evidence.reported_scale: network polygon, rigid blocks, deforming points, triangulation and strain
literature_evidence.source: Official pyGPlates Primer: Deformation and topological networks

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: supports partition-of-unity as a numerical basis concept only; does not provide ARCANA zone geometry or tectonic law
literature_evidence.reported_scale: basis/regularity method, not a geological width
literature_evidence.source: Babuška & Melenk (1997), The partition of unity method

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: junction stability depends on boundary configuration/motion, not incidence alone
literature_evidence.source: McKenzie & Morgan (1969), Evolution of triple junctions

literature_evidence.definition_and_limit: requires boundary classes and evolving kinematic constraints
literature_evidence.source: Cronin (1992), Types and kinematic stability of triple junctions

model_comparison.reason: Avoids unsupported type-specific distinctions; a bounded authorial envelope is explicit, but not yet a physical canonical field.
The current boundary records do not govern a crust-pair classification for each segment.
Opening/closing/shear are diagnostics, not geological boundary-type evidence; no source validates mapping mode to width.
No support exists for correlation length or covariance; adding them would invent parameters.
Cannot stand in for W_model or produce physical strain authority.
